hardwareSolution.Description: Particularly where the Build Construction is 'Proprietary' the Equipment manufacture can use the same hardware Platform for mulitple applications with specific vertical integration points. In order to differentiate this it is common for the hardware solution to have the same name as the application running on it. This is therefore a Product Name. TEMS uses the same approach where the Build Construction is COTS. Where the Build Construction is NFVI/NFCI the phrase 'Multiple Applications' is used.

platform.Description: Generally this is static information as changing the platform conmotes modernizing/replacing the solution. The common name used for the collection of compatible hardware brought together in an architecture. Where the hardware is related to NFVI/NFCI TEMS uses the same values as Build Construction; Where the Build Construction is 'Proprietary' the value represents the name used by the equipment manufacturer for the architectural solution; Where the Build Construction is COTS the model name from the equipment manufacturer is used.

lastTimeBuyExpansions.Description: Towards the end of the product life cycle the manufacturer will announce a last time buy for new deployments. endOfMaintenance.Description: Equipment Manufacturer terminology can vary, but the concepts are the same. There is a period of the product life cycle where the manufacturer actively enhances/optimizes the product making patch releases available in a regular way based on in service performance seen around the deployments across different service providers. In TEMS we call this the Maintenance period. At End of Maintenance the Equipment Manufacturer scales down and no longer provides this active engagement. However, for a period of time they will continue to address specific trouble reports from a Service Provider providing patches to that Service Provider as necessary. In TEMS we call this the Support period. After End of Support the Equipment Manufacurer will no longer address trouble reports raised by a Service provider. It is possible for a Service Provider to pay for Extended Support. If this is the case for a specific Opco it will be specified in another part of TEMS.

assetCategoryId.Description: Within TEMS assets are described in a hieracrhy of Category, Class and Type. Category is the highest level and this is used to differentiate between System Types used as Network Elements, IPT (Customer Care) Applications, Networking Equipment, FCAPS Applications and Office Applications.

buildConstruction.Description: Within TEMS different hardware solutions are categorized by Build Construction. Proprietary - The OEM provides both the Hardware and the Software solution and there is a strong vertical integration between the two. COTS - Where Commercial Off The Shelf equipment is used the vertical integration between software and hardware uses standard APIs so the equipment manufacturers are fully decoupled. Typically it is used with specific solutions where Vodafone (perhaps in conjunction with a third party) have integrated application, middleware and operating system with a COTS hardware solution such as an HP Proliant solution. Voice Core remain responsible for the asset and its life cycle management. Blueprint NFVI/NFCI - A Virtual/Container infrastructure following a Vodafone Defined blueprint architecture and representing a strategic deployment. It hosts multiple applications. The Infrastructure team (Not Voice Core) are responsible for the asset and its life cycle management. Other NFVI/NFCI - A Virtual/Container infrastructure following deployed before the  blueprint architecture solutions were available. They are not strategic deployment and are being phased out - for example Cisco V-Block. It hosts multiple applications. The Infrastructure team (Not Voice Core) are responsible for the asset and its life cycle management.
